# Targets

Read every file at the target's version, without switching branches or checking out a commit, so the working tree stays as it was.

## No target

- The current branch's diff against `git merge-base HEAD <base>`, compared with the working tree by `git diff <merge-base>`, plus the untracked files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`).
- The `<base>` ref is the first that resolves among `origin/HEAD`, the local default branch and the upstream branch, in that order.
- That order holds since the local default branch may hold unpushed commits and the upstream may equal HEAD.
- When none resolves, take `origin/<name>` from the `ref: refs/heads/<name>` line of `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD`, else the first of `origin/main` and `origin/master` that exists.
- An empty diff ends the review with "nothing to review".

## Merge or pull request

- Its diff, description and head commit, read with `glab` or `gh` through read-only commands.
- When the head commit isn't local, fetch `refs/merge-requests/<n>/head` (**GitLab**) or `refs/pull/<n>/head` (**GitHub**) from `origin`.
- Read files with `git show <sha>:<path>` once the head commit is local.
- When the fetch fails, read through the `glab` or `gh` API, in one bulk read rather than one request per file.
- Trace callers yourself with `git show` at the head commit.

## Branch

- Its diff against `git merge-base <branch> <base>`, with `<base>` resolved as for no target, and its files read at its head commit.

## Path, plan, instruction file or pasted text

- The files under the path as they are, or the pasted text, with all their text in scope, since there are no changed lines.
- A plan or an instruction file takes the plan angles.

## Partial access

- When nothing can be read (no repository, no access, an unknown number), stop and say what is missing.
- When only part can be read, take the narrowest safe reading, and say in the final line which reading you took and what is missing.
